description: [Cryptographic & Key Management] Legacy symmetricEncrypt uses ALGORITHM='aes256' (AES-256-CBC) with no auth tag, producing unauthenticated, malleable ciphertext for stored credentials and tokens.
[Cryptographic & Key Management] Key decoded via Buffer.from(key,'latin1'); non-standard Latin1 derivation can misinterpret or truncate the 32-byte AES-256 key, reducing effective key strength.
[Cryptographic & Key Management] symmetricDecrypt uses AES-256-CBC (createDecipheriv) with no integrity check, exposing stored secrets to padding-oracle and bit-flipping tampering attacks.
[Cryptographic & Key Management] 2FA secret decrypted with legacy unauthenticated symmetricDecrypt using shared CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY; a weak cipher mode protects high-value MFA seed material.
[Cryptographic & Key Management] Helpscout webhook HMAC-SHA1 reuses CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY (the AES data key) as a MAC key, violating key separation across distinct cryptographic contexts.
[Authentication & Session] OAuth client secret verified with non-constant-time '!==' string compare, leaking comparison timing that can enable byte-by-byte client_secret recovery.
[Authentication & Session] Email magic-link maxAge set to 10*60*60 (10 hours) despite a 'valid for 10 min' intent; the over-long token lifetime widens the phishing and replay window.
[Transport & Origin] Production CSP script-src includes 'unsafe-inline' and 'https:', undermining the nonce/strict-dynamic policy and re-enabling inline-script XSS execution.
[Transport & Origin] Rate limiter derives client IP from the attacker-spoofable 'cf-connecting-ip' header before request.ip, allowing trivial rate-limit and throttle bypass.
[Transport & Origin] CORS origin falls back to wildcard '*' when ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset in non-production, letting any website send credentialed cross-origin API requests.
[Request Handling] The 'return-to' cookie value is passed to NextResponse.redirect via new URL(value,base); an absolute attacker-set value yields an open redirect to external sites.
[Container & CI/CD] Dockerfile sets ARG NEXTAUTH_SECRET=secret as a default; images built without overriding it ship a predictable session-signing secret enabling JWT forgery.
[Container & CI/CD] ARG CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY=secret default bakes a guessable AES key into the build; unset deploys encrypt all stored credentials and 2FA seeds with a known key.
[Container & CI/CD] docker-compose ships hardcoded Postgres credentials (unicorn_user/magical_password); reused defaults expose the database when deployed unchanged.
[Container & CI/CD] The .env.example commits a concrete CRON_API_KEY hex value rather than a placeholder; copy-as-is deploys grant cron endpoint access via a publicly known key.
[Container & CI/CD] Workflow triggers on pull_request_target with actions:write, exposing a privileged token to fork-triggered runs; mitigated by an explicit maintainer permission check.
[Incoming Webhook & Integration Verification] createWebhookSignature returns '' when no secret is set, so no HMAC is produced and subscribers cannot verify webhook payload authenticity.
[Incoming Webhook & Integration Verification] When the signature is empty the X-Cal-Signature-256 header is omitted entirely, so receivers get unsigned payloads and may accept spoofed events.
[Incoming Webhook & Integration Verification] Helpscout inbound signature checked with non-constant-time '!==' instead of timingSafeEqual used by sibling verifiers, leaking HMAC comparison timing.

[Business-Domain Input Validation] Booking responses use a permissive z.record(dbReadResponseSchema) catch-all that accepts arbitrary keys, weakening allow-list validation of attendee-supplied fields.
[Embed & Cross-Origin Security] Iframe message handler invokes interfaceWithParent[method] gating only on data.originator==='CAL', never validating e.origin, so any window can drive the embed.
[Embed & Cross-Origin Security] Parent SDK 'message' listener fires actions from e.data without checking e.origin against an allow-list, accepting postMessage events from any origin.
[API Version Security Parity] v1 reads credentials from req.query.apiKey (URL query string), leaking keys into logs and history, diverging from v2's Authorization Bearer header scheme.

[Framework-Specific Misconfigurations] Google provider sets allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking:true, linking OAuth logins to accounts by email and enabling takeover if the provider email is unverified.
[Framework-Specific Misconfigurations] A second OAuth provider also sets allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking:true, broadening email-based account-linking takeover risk across identity providers.
